newsitem.title: FINLAND: Metsa-Serla says machines survived fire.
newsitem.headline: Metsa-Serla says machines survived fire.

text.p: Finnish forest-industry group Metsa-Serla Oy said on Thursday that a fire at its paper mill in central Finland caused tens of millions of markka in damages, but injured no one and left the mill's paper machines undamaged.
The fire started at 7.30 a.m. Finnish time (0430 GMT) and was now under control, it said.
"The total damages from the fire are expected to amount to tens of millions of markka," Metsa-Serla said in a statement detailing the damages at its Kangas mill in Jyvaskyla.
The fire broke out in an old warehouse, destroyed the storehouse with about 2,000 tonnes of paper and packaging material, damaged an office building and halted production.
It was probably caused by roof work at the warehouse, Metsa-Serla said.

The mill's paper machine no. 2, which manufactures specialty papers, will resume production in the next few days, but the stoppage on machine no. 4 which produces office paper would last slightly longer, it said.
The mill has an annual capacity of 190,000 tonnes of uncoated fine paper and 70,000 tonnes of specialty grades and daily output is about 700 tonnes, it said.
